items.english: Zenpei stood alone between them, bent on making the two men friends. Hearing the word secretary, Tsunao looked down on Tatsuya as a poor wretch adrift on the waves of the world; hearing the words a graduate of last year in philosophy, Tatsuya laughed to himself at a fool ready to bury a lifetime in the most roundabout empty theory. Zenpei, innocent to the last, took it for certain that they had conceived a respect for each other, and chuckled to himself with delight. "Do show me the keepsake quickly," Mitsuyo said, as if coaxing him.

"We cannot talk at ease here. Shall we go back to the inn and drink a cup together?" Zenpei proposed. "Most excellent," Tatsuya answered on the instant. Zenpei turned. "Tsunao, come along." Tsunao, coldly: "Yes, let us go."

Each with his own thoughts, the four set out. "I shall run ahead for the keepsake," Mitsuyo said, throwing away the wild flowers she had plucked, and ran off like a child. Her skirts fluttering, white chasing scarlet. "Welcome back," came the chorus of voices from the Umeya.
notes: The line on hem, snow and scarlet is a brief lyrical flash with no verb; I have kept it as a visual fragment of white under-robe chasing red, rather than supplying weather or motive the Japanese leaves out.

data.say: Drafted p44 to p47 keeping the paired contempt, Zenpei's pleased misunderstanding, and the childlike run home intact.
